facts.statement: Fossils of Pseudomegachasma have been found in Cretaceous rock layers in Russia and the United States.
facts.quote: It is known from Cretaceous strata in Russia and the United States

facts.statement: Pseudomegachasma is the only known planktivorous member of the Odontaspididae family and the oldest known planktivorous elasmobranch.
facts.quote: It is known from Cretaceous strata in Russia and the United States, and is the only known planktivorous odontaspid, as well as the oldest known planktivorous elasmobranch.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Pseudomegachasma likely evolved from its close relative, the carnivorous shark Johnlongia.
facts.quote: It most likely derived from its closest relative, the piscivorous shark Johnlongia.

facts.statement: The genus was originally named Pseudomegachasma because it was initially thought to belong to the genus Megachasma before being reclassified as an odontaspid.
facts.quote: As its name suggests, it was originally classified under Megachasma, before it was found to be an odontaspid.

facts.statement: Pseudomegachasma belongs to the subfamily Johnlonginae.
Pseudomegachasma is classified within the family Odontaspididae.
Pseudomegachasma is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
Pseudomegachasma lived during the Albian to Turonian stages, approximately 106.3 to 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Turonian (106.3 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Pseudomegachasma is Pseudomegachasma casei.
There are 12 recorded fossil occurrences of Pseudomegachasma in the Paleobiology Database.

rejected.statement: Pseudomegachasma was an extinct genus of filter-feeding sharks closely related to the modern sand tiger shark.
rejected.quote: Pseudomegachasma ("false megamouth") is an extinct genus of filter-feeding shark that was closely related to the modern sand tiger shark.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'closely related to the modern sand tiger shark'
